role: Course-specific Notes layer applied on top of the current Base Notes PM.

instructional_spine.rule: Learning Target and I Can statements define visible instructional clusters. Notes primarily teach current Intro learning; Review/Mastery may appear only when they genuinely support the lesson.

examples_yti.rule: Do not require a fixed six canonical Bank Example/YTI pairs per section. Purpose-author/refine examples and YTIs when Notes are built from the exact target, representations, misconceptions, and current Question Structure. Canonical Bank items may be reused when they are the best anchor.
examples_yti.security: Do not leak official secure Summative or rolling Exit reassessment items into ordinary instructional examples.

reading.benchmark: Mature, concrete, direct, explanatory, relationship-focused high-school prose.
reading.density: A normal substantial reading is usually 3-4 developed paragraphs when the idea warrants it.
reading.vocabulary_first_use: Bold a target vocabulary/notation term the first time it is meaningfully introduced/defined; avoid later clutter.

stop_and_discuss.main_questions: 2-3 content-specific questions; later checkpoints only when useful.

math_notes.abundance: Useful abundance is desirable; teacher may skip.
math_notes.four_forms: When natural, connect Graph + Equation + Table + Context around one coherent relationship.

reading_apprenticeship.opening_sequence: Learning Target/I Can overview -> Vocabulary / Key Notation Preview + sort -> What’s to Come -> Let’s Get Started Notice/Predict/Wonder -> close-reading directions -> I Can 1.

representations.rule: Use applicable forms substantively; no decorative quota.

closing: Summary + Common Mistakes + blank miscellaneous workspace. No embedded official Exit Ticket/Notes Exit Check.
